articles.title: Meet James Bigg, 16-year-old Australian who enters Guinness World Records as world's youngest male software engineer, develops life-saving AI technology
articles.summary: James Bigg from Australia has earned a Guinness World Records title as the world's youngest male software engineer.
articles.body: James Bigg from Australia has earned a Guinness World Records title as the world's youngest male software engineer. At just 16, he works with ResQVision, developing artificial intelligence technology that monitors coastal areas, identifies potential dangers and helps rescue teams prevent drowning incidents.At an age when most teenagers are busy navigating school, friendships and career choices, James Bigg has already made his mark in the technology industry. The 16-year-old from Australia has been recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's youngest male software engineer, proving that age need not be a barrier to pursuing ambitious goals.Also Read| New Jersey teen, 16, turns potato peels and coffee grounds into weedkillerBorn on May 25, 2009, James was verified as a record holder on March 30, when he was 16 years and 309 days old. Now 17, he works as a software engineer at Australian technology company ResQVision, where he is involved in developing artificial intelligence-powered surveillance systems designed to improve public safety and save lives.His work focuses on creating and improving AI software that monitors coastal environments, detects potential dangers and assists rescue personnel in responding to emergencies. For James, the most rewarding part of his profession is knowing that the technology he helps develop can have a real impact on people's lives.James Bigg's journey into software engineering began at 10James' interest in technology began at a remarkably young age. He completed an enterprise networking course when he was just 10 years old. By the time he was 13, he had earned five course certificates and a professional certificate in data science.Rather than waiting until he completed high school to explore higher education, James continued expanding his knowledge by undertaking university-level courses alongside his regular studies.His first professional exposure to the technology industry came through an internship at the age of 15. The experience helped him understand where his interests truly lay, steering him towards hands-on software engineering and artificial intelligence.Today, his responsibilities include writing and testing code, developing products and features, and resolving technical issues. He also interacts with clients to understand their operational requirements, gather feedback and explore how the company's technology can address real-world challenges.Speaking about his work, James explained that developing technology for actual environments requires solutions that are not only innovative but also reliable and practical.How James Bigg is using AI technology to help prevent drowningFor James, his work at ResQVision is also deeply connected to his experiences growing up along the Australian coast. Having witnessed drowning incidents and the dangers associated with coastal environments, he became aware of how quickly emergencies can unfold and how early intervention could help prevent tragedies.As his understanding of artificial intelligence developed, he began recognising the potential of technology to address these challenges.He said, "As I developed my interest in artificial intelligence, I realized that technology could play a meaningful role in addressing these challenges."Explaining what motivates him, James added, "Working at ResQVision allows me to combine my passion for software engineering with the opportunity to contribute to lifesaving technology."He believes AI can play an important role in improving public safety by helping identify risks earlier and enabling rescue teams to make better-informed decisions."For me, knowing that something I've helped develop could contribute to someone returning home safely is incredibly motivating," he said.James presents his AI work at Australian emergency management conferenceJames' growing involvement in the technology sector also saw him present at AFAC26, an Australian emergency management conference, where he discussed the technical development and practical application of artificial intelligence in coastal surveillance and drowning prevention.His presentation covered the results achieved through the technology and its potential to transform how coastal environments are monitored and how emergencies are identified.For a teenager who began pursuing professional technology courses at 10, the opportunity to discuss his work at an industry conference marks another significant milestone.Guinness World Records title is not his only motivationWhile becoming the world's youngest male software engineer is a remarkable achievement, James is keen to acknowledge the people who supported his journey. He credits the engineers and colleagues who shared their knowledge, guided him and helped him develop his skills.Reflecting on his Guinness World Records recognition, he said, "While receiving a Guinness World Records title is an incredible honour, I'm most proud of the meaningful work behind it."He also hopes his journey will encourage other young people to explore their interests without feeling restricted by age or conventional career pathways."You don't have to wait until you're older to start learning, contributing or making a difference," James said.At 16, James Bigg has already combined his interest in technology with a purpose that goes beyond professional recognition. Through his work on AI-powered coastal surveillance, the young Australian is demonstrating how early learning, curiosity and practical innovation can come together to address challenges that affect people's lives.You use AI every day. articles.title: Princess Diana found peace at her brother's South African estate after her divorce; Nelson Mandela-linked £6.75 million property goes on sale with her cottage preserved
articles.summary: A property in Cape Town is attracting attention for more than its size, views or asking price.
articles.body: A property in Cape Town is attracting attention for more than its size, views or asking price. Set within the grounds of the Tarrystone Estate in Upper Constantia, the South African residence has a personal connection to Princess Diana, who used to visit the estate after her separation and divorce from King Charles III. She found privacy there, away from the attention that followed her in Britain, staying in a small thatched cottage on the grounds. As reported by GB News, the estate is now being offered for sale at £6.75 million, with the cottage where Diana spent time reportedly retained much as it was during her visits.Why Princess Diana chose her brother's South African estate for privacyDiana's connection to Tarrystone developed during a difficult period in her personal life. After her marriage to Charles ended, she travelled to South Africa and stayed at the property owned by her brother, Charles Spencer. The estate, located in Upper Constantia, offered a quieter setting, with views towards the surrounding mountains and the ocean.Rather than occupying the main residence, Diana used a separate, thatched one-bedroom cottage within the grounds. The accommodation included its own kitchen, bathroom and living area, giving her a degree of independence from the larger household. According to the account published by GB News, Spencer reserved the cottage exclusively for his sister, and she returned to the estate on several occasions.How Diana's visits to Cape Town became part of the estate's historyThe estate also has a connection to the period when Diana was undertaking humanitarian work in South Africa. During a visit to Cape Town in 1997, she met former South African president Nelson Mandela at Genadendal, his official residence in the city. Their 20-minute meeting focused on the HIV/AIDS crisis in South Africa, an issue Diana had supported through her charitable work and public appearances.Mandela praised Diana for helping challenge the stigma surrounding people living with HIV/AIDS, recalling how her visits to hospital patients had helped change public perceptions of the disease. The meeting took place five months before her death in August 1997.Although the meeting with Mandela took place elsewhere in Cape Town, Diana's visits to Tarrystone Estate remain part of the property's history. The thatched cottage where she stayed has reportedly remained largely unchanged. While parts of the accommodation have undergone renovation, her bedroom has been preserved in its original arrangement. According to a person associated with the estate, Prince William and Prince Harry also visited the property with their mother.How Charles Spencer's own marriage breakdown led him to buy the South African estateCharles Spencer, Diana's younger brother and the 9th Earl Spencer, acquired the South African estate during a period of personal change in his own life. The property provided a place away from the attention surrounding the Spencer family in Britain, particularly as his marriage to his first wife, Victoria Lockwood, was breaking down.The estate included a four-bedroom country residence and several guest cottages. Spencer eventually decided to sell the property following Diana's death and move back to England.Inside the £6.75 million Tarrystone EstateThe property is situated in Upper Constantia, one of Cape Town's established residential areas, with views across False Bay. Its asking price is approximately £6.75 million, according to the sale details reported by GB News.The estate has 10 bedrooms in total, alongside two staff cottages. Its facilities extend well beyond the main accommodation, with a tennis court, a private cinema seating 10 people and a swimming pool designed in a Grecian style. Diana reportedly spent time swimming and sunbathing around the pool during her visits.There are also two vineyards on the grounds. Together, they produce around 300 bottles of wine annually, adding a small-scale wine-making operation to the residential property. Security arrangements include a guard house, CCTV, gated access and electric fencing.What makes Diana's cottage different from the main residenceThe one-bedroom thatched cottage where Diana stayed is separate from the larger house. It has a kitchen, bathroom and living room, making it a self-contained accommodation rather than simply an additional bedroom within the main residence.The cottage has been described as a time capsule because of the decision to retain Diana's bedroom in its original arrangement. According to the source cited by GB News, the rest of the cottage has been renovated, but the bedroom has not been substantially altered.Lynne Baker of Greeff Christie’s International Real Estate, the agency handling the sale, said the property's connection with the Spencer family and Diana contributed to its historical significance. She also pointed to its established place in Cape Town's heritage and the documented history associated with the estate.Disclaimer: This article is based on information published by GB News and other publicly available reports. The Times of India has not independently verified the property's ownership history, asking price, features, historical associations or details of Princess Diana's visits to the estate. Property details and descriptions are based on information attributed to the sources cited and may be subject to change.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Meet Buddy Braley, the 6-year-old who trained his pet goats to collect donations for dog shelters and raised more than $15,000 after losing his own dog
articles.summary: Buddy Braley was just 6-year-old when he found a way to turn the heartbreak of losing his beloved dog into something meaningful for other animals.
articles.body: Buddy Braley was just 6-year-old when he found a way to turn the heartbreak of losing his beloved dog into something meaningful for other animals. Living on a farm near Gloucester in England, the young boy came up with a fundraising idea involving his pet goats, Bella and Bertie. Visitors could feed the animals in exchange for donations, with the money intended to buy beds and toys for dogs waiting in rescue centres. What began as a small roadside effort soon attracted hundreds of supporters, raising more than $15,000 in memory of his companion, Brody.Buddy Braley raised $15,000 for dog shelters with his goatsBuddy’s fundraising effort began with a personal loss that left him deeply upset. His Dalmatian, Brody, had been a close companion who slept beside him every night and looked after him. According to The Washington Post, the dog died at the age of 10 after being diagnosed with bone cancer, with his death coming only days after the diagnosis.For Buddy, the loss was difficult to accept. Rather than simply remembering his pet, he wanted to do something that could help other dogs experience the care and comfort Brody had received.Buddy decided to raise money for local animal rescue centres, hoping to purchase dog beds and toys for animals waiting to find permanent homes. His idea was simple but heartfelt, reflecting the bond he had shared with his own dog.A roadside goat-feeding stand became his fundraising ideaBuddy was already familiar with setting up a small stand outside his family's property, where he sold eggs from their chickens. He used money saved from those sales to buy a large wooden board for his new project.With help from his father, Callum Braley, Buddy cut holes into the board so that his goats could put their heads through it. He painted a farm scene on the structure and trained Bella and Bertie to come when they heard a bell, making it easier for visitors to feed them.The GoFundMe page created by his mother, Abbie Braley, describes how Buddy planned to sell bags of goat food in exchange for donations. The setup allowed visitors to feed the goats while contributing towards beds and toys for rescue dogs.The project took several weeks to prepare. Buddy was particularly fond of goats and had been fascinated by them since he was a toddler, making Bella and Bertie natural companions for his idea.The first donations came from strangers passing the farmThe fundraising stand initially attracted little attention. Buddy sat outside the family property with his goats, waiting for visitors, but nearly an hour passed without anyone stopping.The Washington Post reported that the family's home was in a relatively quiet rural area near Gloucester, where passing traffic was limited. The situation changed when a man stopped to feed the goats and gave Buddy a generous donation of around £60.The contribution surprised the young fundraiser. His mother and her husband were emotional about the gesture, while Buddy struggled to believe how much the visitor had given him.By the end of the day, Buddy had collected approximately £115, equivalent to around $155. His grandmother subsequently shared the fundraiser in a local Facebook group, encouraging more people to visit the farm.Social media helped the campaign reach thousandsThe roadside fundraiser soon attracted attention beyond the family's immediate surroundings. Abbie Braley regularly shares videos of the family's rural lifestyle and animals online, where their combined audience across platforms exceeds two million followers, according to The Washington Post.After she shared Buddy's efforts, people began asking whether they could contribute without travelling to the farm. This prompted her to create an online fundraising campaign through GoFundMe.The original campaign was titled Buddy to be able to buy dog beds and toys for rescue centres. Its initial target was £200, with Buddy hoping to purchase 10 beds and anxiety-relieving teddy bears for dogs struggling in rescue environments.The Washington Post reported that the online donations quickly exceeded expectations, with more than $15,800 raised within days.The growing support meant Buddy could help far more animals than he had initially imagined.The fundraiser also helped Buddy cope with losing BrodyThe campaign carried an additional meaning for the Braley family because animals had already played an important role in Buddy's life.Buddy previously experienced selective mutism, an anxiety disorder that can make speaking difficult or impossible in certain situations. His parents found that spending time outdoors and caring for animals helped him considerably.The family gradually introduced more animals into their rural lifestyle, including chickens, goats and other farm pets. Buddy's relationship with animals had helped him become more comfortable communicating.Brody was particularly important to him. The family's Dalmatian had remained close to the children and was described by his mother as their soul dog.Donations will support rescue centres in needBuddy's original intention was to purchase beds and toys for local rescue centres, particularly for dogs that needed comfort while waiting for adoption.The GoFundMe campaign explained that the family hoped to provide beds for several centres and teddy bears for animals experiencing anxiety. As donations grew, the family began considering how to distribute the money more widely. The Washington Post reported that Abbie and Buddy intended to research which rescue organisations needed the greatest assistance before sharing the funds among several centres.The aim was to reach as many dogs as possible rather than concentrate the donations in a single location. For Buddy, the fundraiser remains closely connected to the memory of his Dalmatian. His motivation was never simply to collect donations but to help dogs that lacked the comfort and companionship he had enjoyed with Brody.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Paris Hilton and her husband rented a $63 million mansion's neighbour for $160,000 a month; their former Beverly Park home is now seeking $159,000 in monthly rent
articles.summary: Paris Hilton and her husband Carter Reum are back in the Beverly Park property market spotlight, with the Los Angeles mansion they once rented for
articles.body: Paris Hilton and her husband Carter Reum are back in the Beverly Park property market spotlight, with the Los Angeles mansion they once rented for $160,000 a month now seeking $159,000 in monthly rent. The couple leased the seven-bedroom residence at 70 Beverly Park in early 2023 while raising their two children, before moving into a neighbouring estate formerly owned by Mark Wahlberg. Hilton and Reum purchased the larger property for $63.1 million in June 2025. The former rental, which features an Olympic-size swimming pool, a tennis court and a separate guest house, is now being offered at a reduced asking rent after previously seeking $195,000 per month.Why did Paris Hilton and Carter Reum choose to stay in Beverly ParkThe mansion at 70 Beverly Park sits in Beverly Park, an exclusive, guard-gated residential community in Los Angeles. According to the New York Post, the enclave is known for its large properties, with each home occupying at least two or three acres. The neighbourhood has also been home to several celebrities, including Justin and Hailey Bieber, Denzel Washington and Adele, who purchased Sylvester Stallone's former residence in 2022.Hilton and Reum signed a multi-year lease for the property in early 2023, after their son, Phoenix, was born in January. Their daughter, London Marilyn Hilton Reum, was born via surrogate in November 2023. The couple reportedly paid $160,000 per month to rent the mansion, remaining there until June 2025. The rental was not available for purchase during their tenancy, and the couple eventually decided to buy a property in the same neighbourhood rather than move away from Beverly Park.Why has Paris Hilton's former Beverly Park rental cut its monthly rent to $159,000The Beverly Park mansion is now being offered for $159,000 per month, down from its earlier asking rent of $195,000 in April. The property has not been available for purchase since its current owner, Los Angeles-based businessman Leonid Smirnov, acquired it for $21.5 million in 2021. The listing is shared by Aaron Kirman, founder and CEO of Christie's International Real Estate Southern California, and Jade Mills of Coldwell Banker.Describing the appeal of the property and its location, Kirman told the New York Post: “Beverly Park is one of the most coveted enclaves in LA, and 70 Beverly Park is a standout. Between the land, amenities and level of security, it’s no wonder celebrities, royalty and billionaires have long been drawn to this community.” He also highlighted the security arrangements within the residential enclave, explaining that the community has 24-hour armed gate security and private patrols.What does the $159,000-a-month Beverly Park mansion look like insideBuilt in 1995, the Mediterranean-style residence spans 14,061 square feet and sits on 3.6 acres. Its layout includes seven bedrooms, nine bathrooms and four powder rooms, along with an elevator. The property also features a six-car garage and additional parking space for 21 vehicles. A circular driveway leads into the estate, while the exterior includes landscaped grounds, walking paths and manicured lawns.The outdoor amenities include an Olympic-size swimming pool, a hot tub, an Astroturf-covered tennis court and a separate guest house. Inside, the residence features a chef's kitchen, a living room with a fireplace and large windows, and a family room with another fireplace and a wet bar. The main bedroom suite has two bathrooms and two walk-in closets, while an upstairs entertainment wing includes a home theatre. The property also has a formal dining room, a games room and a home office.Why did Hilton choose to stay in Beverly Park after losing her Malibu homeAfter renting the neighbouring property, Hilton and Reum decided to purchase their own residence in Beverly Park. In June 2025, the couple moved into Mark Wahlberg's former estate at 71 Beverly Park, paying $63.1 million for the property. The mansion is twice the size of their previous rental, according to the New York Post, and occupies 6.2 acres compared with the rental property's 3.6 acres.The couple's current residence spans 30,500 square feet and also features a swimming pool and tennis court. Speaking about Hilton's decision to remain in the neighbourhood, Kirman told the publication: “She doesn’t want to leave Beverly Park. She looked at a bunch of houses and still landed here.” He added that Hilton appreciated the community's gates, acreage and park. The move came months after the couple lost their Malibu home in the wildfires, according to the report.Disclaimer: This article is based on information published by the New York Post. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, rental price, purchase price, ownership information or other transaction-related claims mentioned. The details should not be interpreted as confirmation from Paris Hilton, Carter Reum or their representatives.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Jonny Huntington suffered a stroke two months after graduating from Sandhurst and spent years rebuilding his ability to walk; he later skied 911km solo to the South Pole
articles.summary: A stroke at the age of 28 left former British Army officer Jonny Huntington paralysed from the neck down on his left side, forcing him to spend years
articles.body: A stroke at the age of 28 left former British Army officer Jonny Huntington paralysed from the neck down on his left side, forcing him to spend years rebuilding his ability to walk. However, the life-changing injury did not end his sporting ambitions. After discovering para-skiing during his recovery and spending five years preparing for an ambitious expedition, Huntington became the first disabled person to ski solo and unsupported to the South Pole. The 38-year-old covered 911km of Antarctic ice in 46 days, overcoming freezing temperatures, difficult snow conditions and the lasting effects of his stroke.How a massive stroke changed his life before the South Pole expeditionBefore his Antarctic achievement, Huntington had served as an officer in the British Army. However, his life changed dramatically when he suffered a stroke at the age of 28. The BBC reported that the incident left him paralysed from the neck down on his left side. The resulting physical limitations meant he had to undergo years of rehabilitation to regain his ability to walk. Although he eventually recovered enough to walk independently, he continued to experience restricted movement down his left side.The stroke also had a lasting impact on his physical capabilities, making the prospect of undertaking an expedition across Antarctica particularly challenging. Huntington had to adapt to life with the effects of the injury and gradually rebuild his physical strength. His recovery eventually introduced him to adaptive skiing, providing an opportunity to pursue competitive sport despite his disability. The experience would later become an important part of his preparation for the South Pole expedition.How adaptive skiing led him to the South Pole expeditionDuring his stroke recovery, Huntington became a member of the Armed Forces Para-Snowsport Team (AFPST). According to the BBC, joining the team ignited his love for skiing and introduced him to a sport that would eventually shape his future ambitions. He subsequently joined the Great Britain para Nordic ski team, competing internationally between 2017 and 2020.His competitive career included World Cup events in Lviv, Ukraine, and Vuokatti, Finland. He also participated in the inaugural European Paralympic Committee Games in Poland in 2020. After eventually stopping competitive skiing, Huntington began considering a different challenge: travelling alone and without support to the geographical South Pole. He spent five years planning and training for the expedition before setting off for Antarctica.How he skied 911km across freezing Antarctic terrainHuntington's expedition required him to cover 566 miles (911km) of Antarctic ice while pulling a 242lb (110kg) sledge containing his food and equipment. He began the journey on 21 November 2024 and had to ski for approximately nine to 11 hours every day. The conditions included freezing temperatures and 24-hour sunlight, making the expedition physically demanding throughout its 46 days.The final stages presented additional difficulties because of huge ice formations known as sastrugi and patches of soft snow, both of which made forward progress harder. His stroke-related disability also affected his ability to manage the physical demands of the journey. Speaking about the difficulties, Huntington told the BBC: "This has been tough, the injury has certainly made it more difficult." He also revealed that, towards the end of the expedition, he had become concerned about whether his stronger right side would withstand the strain.Huntington became the first disabled person to ski solo to the South PoleOn Monday, 6 January 2025, Huntington reached the geographical South Pole after 46 days on the ice. According to the BBC, he became the first disabled person understood to have completed a solo and unsupported ski journey to the destination. At the time of his achievement, only 52 people had successfully skied to the South Pole without support, placing his expedition among a small number of such journeys.Speaking via satellite phone after arriving, Huntington described the experience as emotional. He told the BBC: "It's been a bit of a whirlwind since getting here. It's pretty emotional." He also acknowledged the physical toll on his right leg, which had performed most of the work during the expedition. Reflecting on how he managed to complete the challenge, he said: "On this trip, I kept putting one foot in front of the other until I got to the end." He added: "When things were really tough, I just refused to stop putting one foot in front of the other." Following his achievement, Huntington said he was looking forward to celebrating with a steak and a glass of red wine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Locked and loaded’: Donald Trump warns Iran as Tehran demands US ‘surrender’
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday said the war with Iran was “militarily ...
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday said the war with Iran was “militarily ... effectively over”, signalling that he was not immediately considering a resumption of large-scale attacks, even as he warned that American forces remained ready to strike if circumstances changed.“We're just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters during an unexpected appearance in the White House briefing room after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.Trump said Iran had been “decapitated” but added that Washington was still seeking a long-term arrangement to ensure that Tehran's nuclear programme was dismantled. He described the negotiations as showing “positive momentum” and said there was a “good chance” the conflict could end.Also Read| 'He had no idea she was a spy': Trump backs Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang“They're talking to us, and they're talking very politely, And we'll see what happens,” he said.The president added that military action did not currently appear necessary, although he warned that the US remained prepared to resume operations.“The military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing, but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” Trump said.His remarks were among his clearest indications yet that he was moving away, at least for now, from threats to resume attacks after the US midterm elections.His Republican Party lost control of both chambers of Congress to Democrats in last week's elections, which were marked by public dissatisfaction over the eight-month-old conflict and its impact on fuel prices and the global economy, according to AP.US maintains military blockade as negotiations continueDespite signalling a preference for maintaining the current situation, Trump gave no indication of plans to withdraw the thousands of US troops deployed to waters off Iran or end the naval blockade aimed at restricting Iranian oil exports.“We're keeping it going. We have the greatest military blockade ever,” he said.Trump also reiterated that US forces had identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that could be attacked if military operations resumed. In a phone interview with CNN on Sunday, he said renewed strikes were “highly unlikely” if negotiations made progress and Tehran agreed to a “strong agreement”.The president also said Middle Eastern countries, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait, preferred the current situation.Qatar has been involved in diplomatic efforts surrounding the conflict. According to two Middle Eastern government officials cited by news agency AP, Qatari officials presented proposals concerning Iran's nuclear programme last week.The White House declined to comment on the proposals, although Trump had previously referred to indirect contacts with Tehran.Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani described his meeting with Trump and Vice President JD Vance as “positive” in a post on X.Iran, however, has continued to demand several concessions before entering nuclear negotiations.These include an end to the US blockade on its ports, the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets, compensation for war damage and an end to hostilities across the region, including Israeli military operations in Lebanon.Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected reports of negotiations in a post on X, saying, “The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER. Time to SURRENDER to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out.”Hegseth says next move rests with TrumpEarlier on Monday, US defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the next steps in the conflict were for Trump to decide, including whether Washington would declare an end to military operations while continuing to monitor Iran's nuclear material.Hegseth suggested the president could tell Tehran: “Hey, we're done, and we're going to watch your nuclear material. You better not move it.”The defence secretary has been one of the administration's most prominent defenders of the war.However, the conflict has faced criticism from lawmakers who argue that the administration launched military operations without proper congressional authorisation and violated the War Powers Resolution.Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky moved on Monday to force a vote on impeaching Hegseth, largely over his handling of the war, AP reported.Massie has also accused the defence secretary of knowingly carrying out “unlawful orders” by participating in military action against Iran without congressional authorisation, according to Al Jazeera.Trump has repeatedly threatened to escalate attacks if Tehran does not agree to US terms, but has previously stepped back from military action to allow more time for diplomacy, sometimes following appeals from Gulf allies.The US military has continued limited operations against Iran, including strikes on its air defences at least twice over the past week. It also fired on and disabled a commercial vessel on Saturday, which Washington said had attempted to breach the naval blockade on Iranian ports.US warns citizens against travel to six Middle Eastern countriesSeparately, the US State Department issued its highest-level travel advisory for six countries in the region — Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen — citing security risks and limits on its ability to provide consular assistance.In a post on X, the department said the countries remained under Level 4 advisories, which urge American citizens not to travel there for any reason.“We assign Level 4 based on local conditions and/or our limited ability to help Americans there,” it said, adding: “These places are dangerous. Do not go for any reason.”The department also listed Afghanistan, Russia, Ukraine, Sudan and South Sudan among the 23 countries currently under its highest travel warning.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘How I Met Your Mother’ star Cobie Smulders joined a campaign to protect whales from fishing gear as entanglement is a major threat off the United States West Coast
articles.summary: Whale entanglement in fishing gear off the West Coast of the United States is the focus of the Whales in Crisis public service announcement campaign
articles.body: Whale entanglement in fishing gear off the West Coast of the United States is the focus of the Whales in Crisis public service announcement campaign featuring actress Cobie Smulders. Launched in March 2024 by Oceana, the largest international advocacy organisation dedicated solely to ocean conservation, the campaign calls on decision-makers to do more for marine animals caught in fishing lines along the coasts of California, Oregon and Washington. Entanglement is also a top threat to endangered animals such as humpback whales and leatherback sea turtles, and because most cases go undetected, the confirmed numbers capture only part of the problem.Cobie Smulders lends her voice to the Whales in Crisis campaign against deadly fishing linesAccording to Oceana, Smulders explains in the public service announcement that entangled whales struggle to eat and even to reach the surface to breathe, while the lines cut into their flesh and lead to life-threatening infection and disease. She says the outcome is avoidable and invites viewers to help ensure the animals can swim free. The video and further information are available on the Whales in Crisis webpage.What a severely entangled humpback whale off Baja California reveals about fishing line injuriesUnderwater photographer Alvaro Herrero encountered the humpback whale shown in the campaign off the coast of Baja California in November 2023. Herrero said the animal was covered in millions of sea lice, its spine was bent, its tail was rotting away, and the smell was immense. He said the whale seemed to look at him with sadness, and he hopes the image acts as a wake-up call about what humans are doing to the oceans. His colleagues managed to free the whale from fishing line wound tightly around its tail, but its injuries were deadly. Using information from the gear tag, the National Marine Fisheries Service confirmed that the line came from California’s commercial Dungeness crab fishery.Roughly three in four reported whale entanglements end in death, government estimates showIn 2023, 27 whales were confirmed entangled in fishing gear off California, Oregon and Washington, and five of them were humpback whales caught in California commercial Dungeness crab gear. Government estimates put the death rate for reported whale entanglements at roughly 75%. Geoff Shester, California campaign director and senior scientist at Oceana, said entangled whales can drag heavy lines and gear for weeks, if not months, before succumbing to their wounds. Efforts to reduce harm, including closing fishing zones and cutting the amount of gear in the water, had not brought entanglements within the level allowed under federal law by the time of the campaign launch.Ropeless fishing gear and stricter rules: the solutions Oceana proposed for the West CoastShester said an innovative solution lets fishers catch Dungeness crab in the spring months while protecting whales and sea turtles, because ropeless fishing gear removes the threat of vertical lines. Ropeless gear is also called pop-up or on-demand gear. Oceana called for stricter closures of vertical line gear, comprehensive line marking and new measures to prevent lost fishing gear. In February 2024, Oceana applauded the California Ocean Protection Council for authorising new funding for ropeless technology in the state’s commercial Dungeness crab fishery. The organisation said it would work with fishers, gear manufacturers, fishery managers and enforcement officers on large-scale testing and authorisation of ropeless gear for spring months when waters are closed to conventional gear. It also urged California, Oregon and Washington to strengthen protections whenever conventional gear is used.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ethiopia border violence displaces over 50,000, families flee to Kenya
articles.summary: A harrowing memory continues to trouble Hawa Hassan, who fled her home in Ethiopia’s Moyale region, leaving nearly all her possessions behind.
articles.body: A harrowing memory continues to trouble Hawa Hassan, who fled her home in Ethiopia’s Moyale region, leaving nearly all her possessions behind. She said her house was torched amid the violence, but the incident that remains etched in her mind is the shooting of a 13-year-old girl who was sitting beside a wall.According to Hassan, the girl had not even touched a flag, a detail she cited while describing the tensions over flag displays in the disputed border region. Her account of the teenager’s killing, however, could not be independently verified.The escape into neighbouring Kenya was equally traumatic. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Hassan said several women gave birth while fleeing, while many families arrived without food, cooking equipment or bedding. Newborn babies were left sleeping on bare floors. Cases of diarrhoea were spreading, and families were increasingly worried about malaria as mosquito populations grew.For thousands of people, crossing into Kenya has meant escaping gunfire only to confront another battle for survival. Finding food, shelter and basic necessities has become an immediate challenge. The influx is also placing considerable pressure on Kenyan host communities, where families have opened their homes despite having limited resources and growing fears that the violence could spread across the border.Displacement numbers continue to riseA government-led assessment carried out on October 29 and 30 estimated that 35,950 people had been displaced as of October 24. Of these, approximately 25,000 were living with host families, while nearly 11,000 had taken shelter at temporary displacement sites.The number has increased considerably since then. During a meeting, Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan said the estimated number of people displaced by the fighting had risen from around 36,000 to more than 50,000. The figure includes those staying in temporary settlements as well as people accommodated by relatives and host families.However, the overall displacement figure has not been independently verified, and authorities have yet to establish a final count.The initial assessment covered 758 households and involved government agencies, United nations bodies, the Kenya red cross and other humanitarian organisations. The estimates reflect different reporting periods and should not be treated as directly comparable.The conflict stems from a long-running disagreement over territorial boundaries and administrative authority between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations. Tensions intensified around October 18 following the raising of the Somali regional flag in the disputed Moyale area, highlighting competing claims over the territory.For families arriving in Kenya, however, the political dispute has taken a back seat to more immediate concerns about finding somewhere to sleep and securing food for their children.Humanitarian assistance faces mounting pressureMwasaru Mercy, Kenya's acting commissioner for refugee affairs, told Al Jazeera that a multi-agency government team had been sent to Moyale. The Department of Refugee Services is working alongside local authorities and the United nations high commissioner for refugees (UNHCR) to coordinate relief efforts.However, continued reports of gunfire have raised concerns about further displacement. Many of those arriving urgently require food, shelter, blankets, bedding and mosquito nets."There are no contingency food stocks specifically for this incident because it happened abruptly," Mercy said.The authorities are attempting to mobilise humanitarian agencies and donors to provide assistance. A dedicated refugee camp has not yet been established, as officials want the security situation to improve before taking such a step. Meanwhile, the government is coordinating with UNHCR to register arrivals and assess their requirements.According to Mercy, those affected include Ethiopians escaping the violence, traders and Kenyan residents who have been forced to leave their homes after stray ammunition landed in their neighbourhoods.Fatima Mohammed Cole, UNHCR's representative in Kenya, said women and children account for a significant proportion of the new arrivals. Displaced families are scattered across several locations, including six sites accommodating Ethiopian nationals.The immediate requirements include shelter, food and medical assistance. Overcrowded living conditions have also raised fears of disease outbreaks.Cole said gunfire continued to be heard in Moyale and called for a ceasefire to allow displaced families to return safely to their homes.Relief operations are also taking place on the Ethiopian side of the border. The Ethiopian red cross society said it had distributed emergency shelter materials and essential household supplies worth approximately 30 million Ethiopian birr ($182,970) to 1,000 households displaced from Moyale town and nearby areas.The assistance includes 2,000 tarpaulins, blankets, sleeping mats, dignity kits, water containers, kitchen sets, soap and solar lamps. The organisation said distribution of the supplies was under way. These relief efforts are separate from the humanitarian response being carried out in Kenya.Host communities struggle to copeIn Kenya, residents who initially welcomed displaced families into their homes are finding it increasingly difficult to sustain the support.Abdi Maalim, a member of the Moyale cross-border peace committee, told Al Jazeera that some Kenyan households had moved further inland after bullets and heavy weapons landed close to their homes. He called for stronger border patrols to prevent armed groups from entering Kenyan territory.The influx has significantly increased the burden on local families. Households that previously prepared meals for five or six people are now catering to as many as 20 or 30.Moyale's importance as a major trading route between Kenya and Ethiopia has further complicated the situation. Maalim said trucks transporting goods between Mombasa and Addis Ababa had remained stranded near the border for almost two weeks. Several Kenyan trucks were also stuck inside Ethiopia, while commercial activity in Moyale had slowed considerably.The closure of banks has disrupted the circulation of the Ethiopian birr, adding to the difficulties faced by traders. With the movement of goods restricted, businesses have reported price increases of approximately 20 per cent.Concerns grow over wider regional instabilitySecurity analyst Dr Abdiwahab Sheikh Abdisamad told Al Jazeera that the violence had evolved beyond a local territorial disagreement, exposing deeper ethnic divisions and political rivalry between Ethiopia's regional administrations.He said perceptions of Oromo expansionism, along with allegations that the federal government was supporting Oromia's regional leadership, could further intensify mistrust between communities.The possibility of armed fighters crossing into Kenya, stray ammunition hitting civilian areas and additional displacement has also turned the situation into a security concern for Nairobi, alongside the growing refugee emergency.Kenya's Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, announced that additional security personnel would be deployed along the border to strengthen surveillance and prevent further incidents.During a visit to Moyale on November 5, Kanja said Kenya was in discussions with Ethiopia's federal government to help bring an end to the fighting.He said approximately 10,000 people were living in temporary shelters and public institutions, while others had found accommodation with host families. Kanja also confirmed that a Kenyan national had died after being struck by a stray bullet. A police report indicated that an Ethiopian man had also died from gunshot injuries sustained in Kenya.The figure of 10,000 refers specifically to people staying in temporary shelters and public institutions. It does not represent the total number of displaced people and should not be directly compared with the Kenya Red Cross estimate of more than 50,000, which also includes those living with host families.For Hassan, returning home remains the ultimate hope, but she is unwilling to do so until conditions become safe. For now, she and thousands of other displaced people must depend on local communities and humanitarian organisations for their survival.As the fighting continues, the pressure on host families and already stretched relief operations is expected to grow, making it increasingly difficult to accommodate the growing number of people seeking refuge.Maalim said residents had already exhausted much of their available resources while providing shelter and food to those fleeing Ethiopia."Previously, we were supplying this town alone. Now we are literally taking care of two towns together," he told Al Jazeera.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jimi Hendrix called a tiny London flat his 'only real home'; the rock legend lived next door to a Baroque composer more than 200 years after his death
articles.summary: Jimi Hendrix spent less than a year living in a small London flat, yet the property became one of the most personal places associated with the rock legend.
articles.body: Jimi Hendrix spent less than a year living in a small London flat, yet the property became one of the most personal places associated with the rock legend. Located in Mayfair, the third-floor residence at 23 Brook Street was where Hendrix lived with his girlfriend Kathy Etchingham during the height of his musical career. He reportedly described it as the only home he ever had. Remarkably, the building stood beside the former residence of George Frideric Handel, a celebrated Baroque composer who had lived there more than two centuries earlier.Jimi Hendrix’s London flat became his only real homeThe National Lottery Heritage Fund explains that Hendrix lived at 23 Brook Street between 1968 and 1969, when his career was flourishing. Although he was internationally recognised as a guitarist, the modest flat offered something different from the demands of touring and performing. It became a place where he could settle into everyday domestic life.According to Museums London, Etchingham discovered the flat through an advertisement in a London evening newspaper in June 1968 while Hendrix was in New York. He briefly moved in during July before leaving for an extensive tour of the United States. The couple later returned to the property, where they created a home that reflected their personal tastes.The flat was not simply a temporary place to stay. Hendrix decorated it himself, purchasing turquoise curtains and cushions from John Lewis, alongside ornaments and small decorative objects from Portobello Road Market. These details help explain why the residence became particularly meaningful to him.How did Hendrix discover the composer living next doorThe connection between Hendrix and Handel was more than an unusual coincidence of addresses. George Frideric Handel occupied 25 Brook Street from 1723 until his death in 1759, spending 36 years in the house. As documented by Museums London, the composer created some of his most enduring works there, including Messiah.Handel's former residence was separated from Hendrix's flat by a wall, placing two musicians from vastly different eras in neighbouring properties. The National Lottery Heritage Fund notes that the connection sometimes caused confusion among visitors searching for Handel's home, who would mistakenly knock on Hendrix's door.The museum's account also records that Hendrix eventually became aware of Handel's connection to the neighbouring building. Rather than dismissing the coincidence, he developed an interest in the composer's music and purchased recordings of Messiah and Belshazzar.The restored flat preserves Hendrix's personal surroundingsThe Hendrix flat eventually became an important part of London's musical heritage. Its restoration was undertaken to recreate the atmosphere of the late 1960s, rather than turn the property into an ordinary exhibition space.The National Lottery Heritage Fund reported that the restoration returned the third-floor flat to its 1960s appearance. Personal details, including replicas of the turquoise curtains Hendrix and Etchingham bought from John Lewis, helped recreate the domestic setting. His vinyl record collection also formed part of the experience, connecting visitors with his musical interests and everyday surroundings.The project was supported by a £1.2 million grant from the Heritage Lottery Fund and carried out by the Handel House Trust. The organisation's work brought together the preservation of Handel's historic home and the restoration of Hendrix's comparatively modern flat.According to the Heritage Fund, the Hendrix Museum opened to the public on 10 February 2016, allowing visitors to explore a space that had previously been associated primarily with the musician's private life.Handel's house offers a glimpse into his musical lifeWhile Hendrix's flat captures the atmosphere of the 1960s, the neighbouring house provides a much earlier chapter of London's musical history. Handel Hendrix House explains that 25 Brook Street was where Handel lived, composed and rehearsed many of his works.The composer arrived in London in 1712 and eventually settled at Brook Street in 1723. He remained there until his death in 1759. According to Chronicle Trails, the property was part of a newly developed section of Mayfair and became closely associated with Handel's professional life.The first-floor front room served as a rehearsal room, while another room is believed to have been used for composing. Messiah was among the works associated with the house and was rehearsed there before its first performance in Dublin in 1742.The house also had a social purpose. Handel regularly rehearsed musicians and singers and held informal performances for friends and neighbours. Museums London describes the restored dining room as a place where this musical activity took place, with concerts continuing there today.Two musicians share one historic London addressThe museum now brings both properties together as Handel Hendrix House. The official Handel Hendrix House website describes its mission as caring for and presenting the historic residences of Handel and Hendrix.The museum's expansion also made more of Handel's house accessible to visitors. Chronicle Trails reports that a £3 million project began in 2022, followed by a reopening in May 2023. The institution adopted the name Handel Hendrix House, replacing its earlier name, Handel & Hendrix in London.Handel's residence survived changes in use, including a conversion into a shop in 1905, while Hendrix's flat eventually became part of the museum's administrative space before its restoration. Today, the two adjoining properties stand as reminders of London's ability to attract musicians from different backgrounds and centuries.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Some people take great pleasure in choosing gifts for others.
articles.body: Some people take great pleasure in choosing gifts for others. They remember small details about what a friend likes, spend weeks looking for the right birthday present and feel genuinely happy when someone opens a gift they have picked out. But when the situation is reversed, their reaction can be very different.They may smile awkwardly, insist that the other person should not have spent money on them or immediately say they will get something in return. Even when they like the gift, accepting it can feel surprisingly uncomfortable.This difference may have something to do with how people experience gratitude, reciprocity and the expectations that come with receiving something. While there is no established psychological rule that people who enjoy giving gifts necessarily struggle to receive them, research offers some clues about why accepting a present can sometimes feel less straightforward than giving one.Receiving a gift can create a feeling of obligationOne possible explanation is the pressure to reciprocate. When someone gives us something thoughtful, we may feel that we should do something equally thoughtful in return. Instead of simply enjoying the gesture, we start thinking about what we owe the other person.A 2024 study titled ‘The psychological, computational, and neural foundations of indebtedness’ examined how people experience indebtedness after receiving help or a favour.The researchers explained that receiving something from another person can create both gratitude and a sense of obligation. While gratitude reflects appreciation for what someone has done, indebtedness can make the recipient feel motivated to repay the favour.Why an unexpected gift can make someone uneasyThe discomfort may become stronger when a person has not prepared anything in return. A 2021 study by researcher Julian Givi, published in the Journal of Business Research, examined why gift recipients feel uncomfortable when they cannot reciprocate.Across several studies, Givi found that people giving gifts tended to underestimate how uncomfortable recipients felt when they could not return a present on an occasion when gift exchange was expected. Recipients were more concerned about the imbalance in appreciation than givers often realised.This helps explain why someone might respond to a surprise present by immediately saying, "I haven't got anything for you." Their discomfort may not be about disliking the gift. They may simply feel unprepared for the expectation of reciprocation.Why giving can feel easier than receivingGiving a gift allows a person to decide what to offer, when to offer it and how much effort to put into it. They can choose something that reflects their understanding of the other person and express affection through that action. Receiving is different. The person has no control over what arrives, how much it costs or whether they will be expected to respond in a particular way.Research suggests that gift-giving can also strengthen feelings of connection. A 2015 study examined six studies and found that gifts reflecting the giver's interests could increase feelings of closeness between giver and recipient.The findings suggest that choosing and giving a gift can itself be a meaningful way of connecting with someone. However, the study did not examine whether people who enjoy giving gifts are less comfortable receiving them.It does not mean someone dislikes being appreciatedFeeling awkward when receiving a present does not automatically mean a person has difficulty with affection, low self-worth or a problem accepting love. Some people dislike being the centre of attention. Others worry about the cost of a gift, feel uncomfortable with surprises or come from families and social settings where returning favours is strongly expected.Learning to accept a gift without keeping scoreIf you enjoy giving presents but find yourself uncomfortable when someone gives you one, it may help to notice what is causing the reaction.Separate gratitude from obligation: You can appreciate someone's thoughtfulness without immediately planning an equally valuable return gift.Allow the other person to enjoy giving: A present may be their way of expressing affection, not a request for repayment.Accept the gesture simply: A genuine thank you is often enough. You do not need to explain why the person should not have bought it.Notice what makes you uncomfortable: Is it the attention, the expense, the surprise or the feeling that you now owe something?Giving and receiving are both part of relationships, but they can feel different. For someone who loves choosing thoughtful presents yet struggles when the attention turns towards them, the challenge may not be a lack of affection. It may be learning to accept that affection without feeling that it has to be repaid immediately.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Love Horoscope Today, November 10, 2026: What the stars say about your love life
articles.summary: Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other.
articles.body: Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other. Wouldn't it be nice to know what the universe has planned for you at the beginning of the day? Keep reading to find out if today will be lucky for you.ARIESEvery love tale has its own timing. Singles are cautioned against comparing their road to love with that of another. You are not late, you are not behind. If you’re in a relationship, don’t hold your spouse to some unwritten law on love, since something real takes its time. Your relationship is your own. Let go of all that pressure to fit in. Love is not the speed of a run. It’s a voyage, in fact, end-to-end.TaurusThere is true bonding only where there is respect. If you're single, don't be fooled by charm. The real test is how that person treats you. If you are devoted, tiny acts of respect will not only take away tension but will bring you closer. Listen without interruption, support without judgment. You don have to use big words or make grand gestures. Whenever you feel appreciated love rises automatically.GEMINISlow sparks don’t equal weak sparks. If you’re single, don’t be in a hurry to make a decision. Let it be, so to say, a gradual unfolding. Something real could take a long time to show all its dimensions. If you are devoted, it might be okay to lead through today with quiet steadiness. Don’t waste time pondering how swiftly love is flowing, but pay attention to the signs that your connection is deepening.CANCERLove must be brave, but not all at once. If you're single, take the plunge today - say hello to someone, reply to that message, or smile back. You don’t have to give your whole heart up just yet. If you’re dedicated, discuss something that’s been on your mind recently. Don’t hide it for fear of giving yourself an unpleasant situation. Those little amounts of honesty will build the foundation for deeper trust.LEOThere are arguments in every single bond. The thing that matters is how you fix things. If you're single, don't let one awkward moment keep a grudge. Let others show you that they care. Less fighting, more building of bridges! In a relationship One sincere conversation or one honest gesture can work miracles, silence builds walls. Today’s about mending, not blaming. Love has a way of deepening during the difficult times you guard.VIRGOWhat is left inside keeps growing. If you are single, speak up instead of waiting for the proper time to do so. Honest statements will clear up the confusion. If you are in a committed relationship, never bottle anything up inside. Speak to your heart and your mind. Sometimes your lover will never know what you want or need unless you tell them. Love is more effective when both people can be themselves.LIBRAWords, the day is charged with strength. If you are single, the concept that someone is lovely shouldn't be internalized doing nothing. The words may unlock a door. If you're engaged, something better be happening: your spouse might require some appreciation for what he/she does in the relationship. Do something simple and thoughtful: thank them, give them a compliment. It'll make him/her want to be softer with you.SCORPIOTake a breath and check in with yourself. Are you one? When you are around other people do you genuinely feel seen, or do you merely shrink to fit in? Don't let that feeling go away. If you are in a partnership, assess whether you feel really understood. So today is an excellent opportunity to speak. Show someone how to love you more. If they care, they’ll hear you. You deserve more than an hour or two of attention, you need to feel known.SagittariusLove might be different when sentiments are healed. So if you are single, do not hurry into love only to escape loneliness. Love wholeheartedly, then heal. If you are committed, ask yourself whether you are reacting to your spouse or to your history. Sometimes it’s not them. It might be an old hurt. A little introspection may enable you to learn to love without fear. You have the capacity to modify how you love by changing how you feel.CAPRICORNThe quiet won't be cured by waiting. If you are single do not wait. Be the first to text, be the first to make the first move in talking. That’s powerful enough. If you are in a relationship, that does not mean you are expected to wait for your partner to guess what you want, express it out loud. Reach out, go ahead, get on the phone or give a hug. Love cannot wait, it demands some action today.AquariusYou don’t have to choose between closeness and independence. Well, if you are single, you may seek connection, but also appreciate time to yourself. That would be the right sort of person to grasp it. But if you are dedicated, be honest about your requirements. You may love big but have your own place. Try to offer each other that space on a daily basis, allowing intention to direct it. True love lets you be together, with a little bit of air.PISCESLove may be insisting on your time when you are busy. Single? Reply to the message, express interest or try. Love can't always be perfect on its own time. If you are attached, don't postpone connecting any more. Call. Sit together. Share something true. Small moments matter the most. It's how you say, "I care," when you choose to engage when it's hard. Today, choose a connection — even if it’s a bit of a hassle.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Three workers were killed in an incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, during water tank maintenance work on Tuesday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three workers were killed in an incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, during water tank maintenance work on Tuesday.State minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana expressed grief over the deaths and said she had spoken to the district administration to ensure assistance for the affected families."Deeply saddened by the tragic loss of three precious lives in the incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur...I have spoken to the district administration and directed them to extend all necessary support to the affected families and ensure that the situation is addressed with utmost urgency," she said.The safety and dignity of every worker must remain paramount. This tragic incident will be thoroughly investigated, and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings. We must ensure that every necessary measure is put in place to prevent such tragedies from recurring," the minister added.Keerthana said the incident would be investigated and appropriate action taken based on the findings.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
